person: Devon Clarke is 26, eight months into his first nonprofit finance job after leaving an audit team, and runs finance at a twenty-person youth tutoring and family services nonprofit in Dayton, Ohio. This is the first federal drawdown and SF-425 he has owned alone; his predecessor left a binder and spreadsheet tabs named FINAL and FINAL2. The quarter ended September 30 and the audit is four months out, with the executive director having told the board all is in order. He wants to understand every step well enough to explain it to the ED in one paragraph, and he wants nothing certified to the government without his explicit approval.
stated_up_front: Hi, I need to do the draw and the SF-425 for our Department of Education youth tutoring grant for the quarter that ended Sept 30. It's my first one on my own, so please show me the rule behind each cost you include or leave out, and don't submit anything until I've approved it.

facts.truth: Federal tutoring grant, period October 1, 2025 to September 30, 2028, reimbursement-only; the quarter in question is July 1 to September 30, 2026.
Through June 30, 2026 the organization has drawn $182,400 cumulative; the July draw of $6,150 was for 15 laptops for tutors.
The Q2 2026 (June 30) report was filed by his predecessor on a cash basis showing $182,400 cumulative outlays.
A reading curriculum license for $9,800 was paid in August 2025, before the award began, and was recoded to the grant in a later cleanup.
A $1,340 wine and catering invoice for the volunteer appreciation dinner in August, plus a $2,500 deposit for the spring fundraising gala, both coded to the grant.
A $750 IRS penalty for a late Form 990 is coded to the grant, as is a $3,000 state association assessment whose letter says it is all used for lobbying.
The July to September office rent of $7,200 belongs to the county family services award but was coded to the tutoring grant.
A $4,260 workbook invoice dated September 18 is still unpaid, due in November.
Payroll allocates the development director, Marcus Hale, 40% to the grant, about $9,600 for the quarter, but his certified timesheets show 100% fundraising.

facts.about: Allowable paid costs he is sure of
facts.truth: Tutor salaries and fringe of $58,300 for the quarter match timesheets, plus $2,115 paid for tutoring supplies on September 5.

unknowns: Whether the award's terms require prior approval for equipment purchases like the laptops or the supplies.
What indirect cost rate, if any, the notice of award allows him to charge.
Whether the $3,000 assessment can be partly allowed if the association has other activities.
Whether the SF-425 is due by a deadline that has already passed or is still days away.
